LESSON: CITIZENSHIP IN KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Systems
Topic 4.3: Citizenship in Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Citizenship in Kenya, part of Political Systems in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we promote responsible citizenship?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Citizenship in Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Citizenship in Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social wellbeing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Citizenship in Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate being a good citizen in the community. • In groups, learners discuss ways of becoming a Kenyan citizen. • Learners are guided to use digital resources with assistive technology to find out ways of becoming a Kenyan citizen and share in class. • In groups, learners to debate on dual citizenship in Kenya. • With peers, learners are guided to develop communication messages on good citizenship in our country. • In groups, learners are guided to write an essay on what may happen if one lost Kenyan citizenship. • Learner is guided to create and recite poems on Kenyan citizenship. • In groups, learners develop intergroup communication skills for promotion of peaceful coexistence as they develop communication messages on good citizenship and share with others in school. How can we promote responsible citizenship?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Citizenship in Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Citizenship in Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: Learners practice self-drive as they discuss in groups, ways in which one may lose Kenyan citizenship and present in class.

• Citizenship: Learners develop intergroup communication skills for promotion of peaceful coexistence as they develop communication
